content:
# Browser session and route ownership

The shell checks the initial session before exposing a protected route. It rechecks `/me` when a signed-in user returns to a visible tab or restores a page from the browser's page cache. Concurrent return events share one check; hidden tabs and anonymous pages do not poll. The footer also offers Check session and shows the last successful check. Network errors remain visible without erasing the account or automatically repeating a mutation. Each session check has a ten-second deadline, cancels its request and settles even if a transport ignores cancellation.

A confirmed 401 removes the account and organization context and renders sign-in at the existing protected URL. Signing in returns to that destination through the existing validated authentication destination. This security boundary unmounts the previous page, including any local unsaved draft. A confirmed different account clears the previous organization and remounts the current route for the new identity. Every result belongs to the exact account object captured when its check began; replacement, logout or shell disposal cancels that ownership, so a late reply cannot restore a departed identity. Transport cancellation is separate from result ownership.

Route headings may arrive after a resource request. The shell tracks heading creation and text changes to update the document title. It initially lands keyboard focus on the content region, then moves focus to the first heading only if the user has not deliberately moved it elsewhere. Route departure disconnects the old observer. The actual Chromium proofs hold a resource response, preserve deliberate keyboard focus, abandon a delayed route and sign out through a second native tab; pure tests cover request coalescing, expiry, failure recovery, account replacement, malformed replies, deadlines and disposal.
